title: Balasore: looking closely, asking further
scope_notice: This reading accompanies the journey below. Saved journeys and downloads retain the complete original chapters and practical prompts.

paragraphs.text: What can looking tell us, and when do we need another kind of evidence? Carry that question through these three chapters. A photograph, a passage of fiction and an answer at the table each invite attention, but they answer different questions.

In a 2020 Chandipur study, Sourav Dey and colleagues collected sediment from eleven locations, dried it and separated grains with sieves. Their samples near the beach were generally coarser than those near the estuary. Looking at the shore and measuring its material are different kinds of observation; these results do not identify the sand in our photograph or establish safe access.

Bring the same care to the reading chapter. When a narrator makes a judgement, ask whose voice you are hearing and what details support it. Keep a note of the edition and translator alongside your response. A fictional scene can sharpen a question without becoming a record of what happened at a particular address.

At the table, begin with a question that someone can answer: how is this dish prepared here? Let the answer belong to that cook and that meal. You need not turn it into a claim about every kitchen along the coast. Give each chapter room to change what you notice, without making the three into a timed circuit.

sources.title: Dey, Sen and Dey (2020)
